acceptance_checks.check_id: Timestamp exposes unix_seconds() and subsecond_nanoseconds() accessors and an associated UNIX_EPOCH value without acquiring the current time.
acceptance_checks.detail: The public API exposes UNIX_EPOCH, checked from_unix_parts, unix_seconds, and subsecond_nanoseconds without acquiring a clock.

acceptance_checks.check_id: Timestamp supports Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, and Hash; focused tests confirm ordering across negative pre-epoch values, UNIX_EPOCH, positive values, and adjacent nanosecond boundaries.
acceptance_checks.detail: Timestamp derives the required deterministic value traits and focused tests verify ordering and value behavior.

acceptance_checks.check_id: Timestamp uses one normalized in-memory representation: signed Unix seconds plus subsecond nanoseconds in the inclusive range 0..=999_999_999; the seconds component is the mathematical floor second for negative instants, so each represented instant has one value representation.
acceptance_checks.detail: Timestamp uses signed Unix mathematical floor-seconds plus normalized non-negative nanoseconds, giving a unique represented value for each supported instant.

acceptance_checks.check_id: Timestamp::from_unix_parts rejects subsecond_nanoseconds >= 1_000_000_000 with TimestampError::NanosecondsOutOfRange { actual } and does not normalize, truncate, wrap, or silently alter input.
acceptance_checks.detail: from_unix_parts rejects every subsecond nanosecond value >= 1_000_000_000 without normalization, truncation, wrap, or silent alteration.

acceptance_checks.check_id: TimestampError is bounded metadata-only and never carries source text, clock/provider state, or platform-specific error payloads.
acceptance_checks.detail: TimestampError contains only the rejected u32 nanosecond value and no source text, provider/clock state, or platform payload.
